name: ghome
description: See and control the lights and plugs in your own Google Home, through the open-source ghome CLI.
long_description: Ask Claude what is in your Google Home, whether a device is on, and to set one light, plug or wall switch, or the lights of one room. Four tools: ghome_devices and ghome_device_state read; ghome_device_set and ghome_room_lights change what you name, and Claude asks you before each call. No tool can reach a lock, a garage door, a heater, a camera or a speaker's volume, remove or rename a device, edit a room or a routine, make an announcement, or touch your account. The extension asks for no password: first install the ghome CLI and run `ghome auth login` in a terminal, which stores the credential in your OS keychain. The bundled ghome reads it from there and caches a short-lived token beside it. When the credential ends, the tools say so; run `ghome auth login` again. What the tools return goes to Claude as part of your conversation. On macOS the first call asks for keychain access, and a new token asks to write it back; choose Always Allow for each. A new version of the extension is a new program to the keychain and can ask again. Unofficial; not affiliated with or endorsed by Google. It uses the private API behind the Google Home app, which Google can change at any time.

tools.name: ghome_devices
tools.description: What devices you have: name, kind, room, online, and what the tools can change on each.

tools.name: ghome_device_state
tools.description: Whether a device is on, with its brightness and color, and whether a lock is locked.

tools.name: ghome_device_set
tools.description: Set one named light, plug or wall switch: on or off, brightness, color or color temperature, and return the state read back.

tools.name: ghome_room_lights
tools.description: Set the lights of one named room, and nothing else in it, and return each light's state read back.
